title: Incident Bot v2: Config diff fetcher + redaction for customer-safe Slack rendering
creator: Miles Thornton
content:
## Summary
Build the Incident Bot v2 “Config changes” context card by:
1) retrieving a tenant-safe config diff for the affected service/region/time window, and
2) applying robust redaction + allowlisting so no secrets or customer-sensitive values are ever emitted to Slack.

This ticket covers the bot-side fetcher, formatting, and the redaction layer used before any Slack rendering. The backing config diff endpoint/auth wiring is tracked separately (platform work), but we must define the contract and implement guardrails here.

## Why
Recent incidents show responders spending 10–30 minutes manually hunting for routing policy/feature flag/quota changes that correlate with 5xx and latency regressions. We want to standardize “first 5 minutes” context without leaking tenant data.

Primary goals:
- Surface *what changed* (high-signal keys only) alongside deploy + saturation cards.
- Ensure diffs are customer/tenant-safe (redacted, allowlisted, audited).
- Degrade gracefully when the diff source is slow/unavailable or access is insufficient.

## Requirements
### Functional
- Bot can fetch config diffs for an incident context (service, env, region, tenant scope).
- Slack card shows:
  - a short summary (N changed keys, most important categories)
  - top changes preview (truncated)
  - actions: “View full diff (modal)”, “Copy CLI command”, “Open Console diff view” (deep link if available)
- Diff categories of interest (must be supported in summary/filters):
  - feature flags / rollout state
  - routing policy / fallback policy
  - quota / rate-limit knobs
  - model pins / model variant preferences

### Security / data handling
- Secrets never appear in Slack output.
- Redaction must happen in-process before Slack rendering, even if upstream says “already redacted”.
- Only allowlisted config namespaces/keys are eligible for showing *values*. Everything else should show key names + “(redacted)” or “(not allowlisted)”.
- Any value that looks like a secret should be redacted regardless of allowlist.
- Emit audit events (handled by platform endpoint; bot must include request context for correlation): incident_id, requester (Slack user), channel, tenant_scope, reason (“incident_context”).

### Reliability
- Bot response within 2s for initial card rendering.
- If diff fetch > 1.5s, render card in “degraded” state with cached last-known diff (if any) + deep links.
- Cache diffs per (service, region, tenant_scope, time window) with TTL to reduce repeated modal opens.

## Proposed design
### Data contract (bot-side assumptions)
Bot will call an internal endpoint (exact path TBD by platform) that returns a normalized diff:
- changes: list of { path, before, after, change_type }
- metadata: { from_revision, to_revision, change_time_range, config_source }

Bot must treat this as *untrusted* for Slack safety: we re-run redaction + allowlisting.

### Redaction strategy
We apply two layers:

1) **Hard redaction (secret detection)**
Always redact values that match any of:
- Key name patterns (case-insensitive):
  - *secret*, *token*, *api_key*, *apikey*, *password*, *passwd*, *bearer*, *authorization*, *private_key*, *client_secret*, *session*, *cookie*, *signing*, *hmac*
- Value patterns:
  - PEM blocks (-----BEGIN …-----)
  - JWT-like tokens (three base64url segments separated by '.')
  - High-entropy strings over length threshold (heuristic; see below)
  - Known cloud credential prefixes (best-effort):
    - AWS: AKIA…, ASIA…
    - GCP service account JSON indicators ("private_key", "client_email")

2) **Allowlist gating (customer-safe fields)**
Only show raw values for keys under allowlisted namespaces, with additional per-key rules:
- allowed examples (initial set; can tune based on incidents + security review):
  - routing.policy.* (excluding any embedded headers)
  - routing.fallback.*
  - limits.rate_limit.*
  - limits.quota.*
  - feature_flags.* (values may be boolean/percentage/variant)
  - model_pins.* (model IDs only; redact any customer prompt templates)

Everything else:
- show key path
- show change type (added/removed/modified)
- show “value redacted (not allowlisted)”

Heuristic for entropy-based redaction:
- If value is a string > 24 chars and Shannon entropy estimate > ~3.5 AND contains mixed classes (upper/lower/digit/symbol), treat as secret.
- Always redact if string > 64 chars unless key is explicitly allowlisted AND passes “safe value type” checks.

Safe value types for allowlisted keys:
- boolean
- small integers
- small floats
- enums from a fixed set (e.g., routing mode = ["cost", "latency", "balanced"])
- model IDs matching `^[a-z0-9._-]+$` and <= 64 chars

### Slack rendering rules
- Default card shows up to 8 changes (prioritize allowlisted + high-signal categories first).
- Truncate each rendered line to avoid wrapping; include “+N more changes” indicator.
- Modal view paginates changes (50 per page) with the same redaction applied.
- Prominent warning banner if any redaction occurred: “Some fields hidden for safety. Use Console diff view for authorized access.”

### Failure modes
- 403/insufficient scope: show card with “Diff unavailable (permissions)” and link to runbook/break-glass path.
- 404/no diff available: show “No config changes detected in last X minutes” (still provide manual commands).
- timeout: show cached diff if available; otherwise render links only.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Config diff card renders with summary + preview + actions.
- [ ] All Slack output passes redaction + allowlist gating (unit tests cover representative secrets).
- [ ] Redaction tests include:
  - PEM/JWT
  - AWS-like keys
  - long high-entropy strings
  - keys named *token*/*secret* etc.
  - allowlisted keys with safe vs unsafe values
- [ ] Modal view uses same redaction logic as card preview.
- [ ] Degraded mode works (timeout -> cached/links), no Slack action failures.
- [ ] Security review sign-off recorded (Marcus Lin / Naomi Feldman).

## Implementation notes
- Implement redaction as a pure function with explicit inputs/outputs and a reason code per field:
  - REDACTED_SECRET_PATTERN
  - REDACTED_NOT_ALLOWLISTED
  - REDACTED_UNSAFE_VALUE_TYPE
- Keep an internal debug log (not Slack) with counts only, not the redacted content.
- Add a config-driven allowlist to avoid code deploys for every tuning change; default deny.

## Open questions
1) Canonical time window for diffs in incident context: last 30 min vs since incident start?
2) Should we show “who changed it” if available? (May be sensitive; likely Console-only.)
3) Do we support tenant-scoped diffs for Dedicated/Private where config lives in separate stores?

## Links
- Confluence: incident-bot-diagnostics-v2-design (config diff section)
- Drive: config-diff-api-notes
- Related tickets: ENG-5421 (recent deploys), ENG-5423 (saturation), ENG-5426 (scopes/audit)

## Rollout plan
- Behind feature flag `incident_bot.v2.config_diff_card` (beta cohort = SRE rotation only).
- First enable in 1–2 regions (us-east, eu-west) and Hosted API services only.
- Monitor:
  - redaction rate (percentage of changes redacted)
  - card render latency
  - modal open success rate
  - any security reports / suspected leaks (P0 rollback)

## Definition of done
- Code merged + shipped behind flag
- Unit/integration tests passing
- Security review approval attached
- Runbook snippet updated to include "Config diff" card interpretation + break-glass path
comments: 2025-02-13 (Miles Thornton): Marking P0. We had multiple incident threads where config change correlation was purely manual. Need bot-safe diff ASAP but must be bulletproof on redaction.
2025-02-14 (Kaitlyn Nguyen): Please ensure bot treats upstream as untrusted. Redaction must happen in bot service before Slack. Also we need a default-deny allowlist, not blocklist.
2025-02-18 (Jacob Stein): Drafted redaction function + initial allowlist. I’m adding tests for JWT/PEM/AWS keys. Will also add entropy heuristic but want Security to sanity check thresholds.

2025-02-20 (Marcus Lin): For entropy heuristics, be conservative. Prefer hard patterns + key-name matching, and cap max visible string length even when allowlisted. Also ensure we never log raw values in bot logs.

2025-02-25 (Devon Price): Slack modal pagination already exists in v2 branch; can reuse. Needs a stable cursor key per diff page (hash of redacted diff + page index) to avoid mismatched pagination when cached.
2025-03-01 (Benji Okafor): Platform endpoint will include `before/after` fields as strings. Bot should parse types only for allowlisted keys; otherwise treat as opaque and redact.
2025-03-04 (Allison Grant): Suggest prioritizing changes to `routing.*`, `limits.*`, and `feature_flags.*` in the preview ordering. That’s what responders look for first.

2025-03-06 (Jacob Stein): Implemented allowlist gating + secret pattern redaction; added 18 unit tests. Next: wire caching + degraded mode and add integration test for a ‘not allowlisted’ diff rendering.
